verdict.rationale: Browser Use ships a separate open-source Python library that runs the agent locally from your own code, and a community user confirms running it locally against their own browser. However, the docs present the Cloud Agent/Browser APIs as distinct, and hardened stealth Chromium, residential proxies and automatic CAPTCHA solving are documented as cloud-only, so the full product is not shown as self-hostable. Missing for 10: self-hosting of the cloud agent/browser infrastructure, explicit license and deployment documentation for the library, and parity of cloud features (stealth, CAPTCHA, profiles) in the self-hosted form.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: For a local agent, use the [open-source library](/open-source/quickstart).
Want to automate the web at scale, from your own code, and with any LLM? Use the Python library
Documentation for Browser Use Cloud Agent and Browser APIs, and the separate open-source Python library
If you run it locally, you can connect it to your real browser and user profile where you are already logged in.
